title: Home Mortgage Loans: Assessment of Late Charges
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Assessment of Late Charges

A late charge on Home Mortgage Loans is a fee added to what the borrower owes when an installment is not received in full in time. This policy settles when an installment becomes subject to the charge, how much the charge is, and when no charge may be made at all.

## When the charge arises

An installment attracts a late charge if it has not been received in full by the close of the program's grace period, which runs for the program's number of grace days in calendar days following the installment's due date.

- **Start of the count.** The due date is the one the bank's records show for that installment. The calendar day after that due date is grace day 1.
- **Moment the charge attaches.** The charge applies only when the installment is still unpaid after the last grace day has ended. Receipt in full on the last grace day itself is in time.
- **Evidence.** Whether and when the installment was received is taken from the loan's payment records, not from the borrower's recollection.

## Amount of the charge

The late charge is the principal-and-interest payment of the installment multiplied by the late charge percentage that the program sets for the borrower's state of residence, divided by 100, and rounded half-up to the cent. The escrow part of the installment never forms part of this base.

## Where no charge is made

- An installment carries no more than one late charge, however long it stays unpaid.
- While the loan is in forbearance, no late charge applies.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical grace period of 10 days)

The grace length, dates and percentage below are invented for the illustration; the real grace days and percentages are those published for each program.

| Due date | Last grace day | Installment received in full | Late charge |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 11 June | on 11 June | none — received within grace |
| 1 June | 11 June | still unpaid when 11 June ends | applies from 12 June |
| 1 June | 11 June | still unpaid on 30 June, a charge already made | no second charge for that installment |

## Amount example (hypothetical)

An imagined installment has a principal-and-interest payment of $1437.89 and an escrow payment of $410.00. Under an imagined percentage of 3.5 for the borrower's state, the base is $1437.89 alone; multiplying by 3.5 and dividing by 100 gives $50.32615, which rounds half-up to a charge of $50.33.
